reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When we want to model decisions in a network, we often need to turn any real number into a probability between zero and one. If an input grows very large or very negative, we want the output to saturate rather than grow without bound. The logistic function provides this smooth transition, mapping the entire real line into a bounded range. By adjusting its steepness and midpoint, we can shape how quickly this transition happens and where it centers.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function maps any real number into the range between zero and one. Adjust the steepness $k$ and midpoint $x_0$ to see how the S-curve shifts and stretches.
reply.instructions: Adjust the sliders for steepness and midpoint to change the shape of the S-curve. Observe how the output and slope update at the marked point.
